chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash your garment from the urine of that whose flesh is not eaten.'

key_terms.لَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: whose flesh is not eaten (referring to non-halal animals)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for cleaning clothes soiled with the urine of non-halal animals?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the purification method for garments soiled by the urine of non-halal animals, distinguishing them from halal ones which often require only sprinkling or wiping in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the practical application of *taharah* (ritual purity) laws, emphasizing that the urine of animals like camels or cows (if considered non-halal in specific contexts) or wild beasts requires full washing (*ghusl*) to remove impurity (*najāsah*). This ruling is foundational for understanding the nuanced differences in *fiqh* regarding various animal excretions.
